answers.10_evidence_scopes: Results are explicitly separated into baseline, official-checkpoint custom stress, component stress, local/external pipeline evidence, diagnostic, oracle, and upper bound.
answers.1_are_defenses_merely_tool_name_classifi: No. Official checkpoints and structural methods resist some simple surface shifts, but they remain incomplete on the joint decision.
answers.2_simple_surface_shift: TS-Guard, IPIGuard alias-normalized DAGs, and CaMeL synchronized rewrites resist selected simple shifts.
answers.3_effect_sensitive: Some methods are effect-sensitive, but not jointly safe: local-Qwen semantic mapping reaches effect sensitivity 0.833, while topology-only IPIGuard exposes no effect decision.
answers.4_authorization_sensitive: Authorization sensitivity remains incomplete: local-Qwen reaches 0.375, Safiron is weak in Phase 4, and topology-only IPIGuard is not evaluable.
answers.5_resource_binding: Resource binding is a distinct bottleneck: local-Qwen resource sensitivity is 0.125, despite stronger effect sensitivity.
answers.6_utility_preservation: High refusal is separated from safety; local self-audit and some policies pay substantial utility or denial cost.
answers.7_structural_defense: Structural defenses improve format stability but do not by themselves establish joint effect-resource-authorization reasoning.
answers.8_ipiguard_semantic_layer: The deterministic mapper avoids unsafe pre-allow by abstaining on 0.579 of cases and has effect sensitivity 0.375; local-Qwen raises effect sensitivity to 0.833 and coverage, but unsafe pre-allow rises to 0.333. This supports a missing semantic-decision-layer diagnosis, not a solved guard.
answers.9_camel_misses: Current CaMeL custom-core unsafe misses are concentrated in control-dependency cases (6 misses).
